newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strike threat in German printing industry averted.
newsitem.headline: Strike threat in German printing industry averted.

text.p: Germany's IG Medien trade union said on Thursday it had reached a wage deal for the 130,000 workers in the sector, averting the threat of all-out strikes across the industry.
"We have a result," IG Medien negotiator Franz Kersjes told reporters as he emerged from the talks.

Union officials later said the deal included a 1.5 percent pay rise this year and an agreement not to implement a new law cutting sick pay entitlements by 20 percent of salary. However, end-of-year employee bonuses will be cut by five percent.
More than 20,000 print workers have been involved in industrial action against the cuts in labour costs that employers had been demanding.
Major German newspapers and printing groups, including the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung and the Axel Springer Verlag AG publishing group, were hit by the stoppages.
Had the talks collapsed without an agreement, IG Medien would then have started ballotting workers for all-out strikes.
